patches.value: Babin–Ilyin–Titi primary results in their normalized mean-zero homogeneous spaces on R/(2 pi Z): write U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, Uhat(k)=exp(-it k^3) z_k(t), so z'_k=(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k}exp(3it k k1 k2)z_{k1}z_{k2}. A weak solution satisfies this integrated equation at every nonzero k. For every s>=0, B0>=0, horizon b>0 and initial z0 in dot H^s with ||z0||_2<=B0, the Galerkin equations z'_k=Pi_m[(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k} exp(3it k k1 k2)(Pi_m z)_{k1}(Pi_m z)_{k2}], z(0)=z0, have a bound sup_{[0,b]}||z^(m)||_{dot H^s}<=K_s(b,B0,||z0||_{dot H^s}), uniformly in m; the proof supplies a bound uniform when the indicated initial norm is bounded. For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];dot H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L-infinity dot H^s to a weak solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique and C([0,b];dot H^s), with Lipschitz continuous dependence in dot H^s, and conserves L2 at every time: for s>1/2 by the regular-solution uniqueness theorem, for 0<s<=1/2 by the positive rough-solution uniqueness theorem. For s=0 there is likewise a unique C([0,b];L2) weak solution with Lipschitz dependence. For any theta in (-1,0], and any two flows with ||z0||_2+||w0||_2<=B0, sup_{[0,b]}||z-w||_{dot H^theta}<=C' C_{B0}^b ||z0-w0||_{dot H^theta}, where C',C_{B0} depend only on B0,theta. The real, zero-mean class and normalized measure are standing conditions throughout.

Li–Wu continuous trilinear estimates: Let 0<=lambda<=1, b>=a>=0, b-a<=1, and f_j in L-infinity([a,b];H^lambda), partial_t f_j in L-infinity([a,b];H^(-23/14)), j=1,2,3. The operator C_[a,b] of D019 satisfies ||C_[a,b](f1,f2,f3)||_{L2} <= C(b-a) product_j ||f_j||_{X([a,b])}+C||f_i||_{L-infinity H^(-23/14)} product_{j!=i}||f_j||_{L-infinity L2}, for each i=1,2,3. If all inputs are time-independent, ||C_[a,b](f1,f2,f3)||_{L2}<=C_lambda(b-a)^lambda product_j||f_j||_{H^lambda}. In this source statement all spatial norms are Li–Wu's unnormalized norms, equal to sqrt(2 pi) times D003 norms, including X. Constants are independent of the time location and Fourier support.

Li–Wu product and bilinear-stage estimates: For 0<lambda<=1 define a(lambda)=1/2-lambda if lambda<1/2, any fixed positive epsilon if lambda=1/2, and 0 if lambda>1/2. Then ||fg||_2<=C_lambda,epsilon ||f||_{H^lambda}||g||_{H^{a(lambda)}}. For mean-zero time-independent f1,f2 in H^lambda and a step [t_n,t_n+tau] with tau>0, the bilinear stage G_n(t;f1,f2)=(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f1,f2) ds satisfies ||G_n(t;f1,f2)||_{H^beta}<=C tau^((1+lambda-beta)/(1+lambda-beta0))||f1||_{H^lambda}||f2||_{H^lambda}, beta0<=beta<=1+lambda, uniformly on the step. Here beta0=2lambda-3/2 if lambda<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon if lambda=1/2 with an arbitrary fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0, and beta0=lambda-1 if lambda>1/2. All source spatial norms are sqrt(2 pi) times ours; constants depend on exponents and chosen epsilon but not on n,tau or support.

Li–Wu's exact algebraic scheme identities: for smooth mean-zero f, on [t_n,t_n+tau], the stage F_n in D022 and cubic stage C_n in D024 obey A^n[f]=C_n(t_n+tau;f)=H^n[f]+R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f), where R2 has the exact Fourier covariance formula D014. The numerical step v^{n+1}=v^n+F_n(t_n+tau;v^n)+H^n[v^n] becomes exactly Psi_tau in D011 after v^n=S_{-t_n}u^n; the quadratic and cubic physical increments are exactly D009 and D010, with their displayed coefficients and endpoint signs. Equivalently S_{-(t_n+tau)}Psi_tau(S_{t_n}f)=f+F_n(t_n+tau;f)+C_n(t_n+tau;f)-R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f). No convergence estimate is asserted in this input.
